title: When a goal is off track: four levers
objectives: Use the four levers in order, and never chase returns to catch up.
Say which lever fits a must-have vs a should-have goal.
body_md:
Invest more: raise the SIP or add a lump sum (bonus, maturity). Extend the date: retire two years later; buy the house a year later. Adjust the target: a smaller car, a less expensive college option. Review the mix: only if the current mix is clearly too conservative for the horizon; never chase returns to catch up.

| Lever | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Invest more | Raise the SIP or add a lump sum (bonus, maturity) |
| Extend the date | Retire two years later; buy the house a year later |
| Adjust the target | A smaller car, a less expensive college option |
| Review the mix | Only if the current mix is clearly too conservative for the horizon; never chase returns to catch up |
example: Retirement goal 30% behind plan: raise the SIP, extend the date by two years, or trim the target — never move a near goal into small caps to catch up.
say: Off-track is fixed by levers, not gambling.
Never chase returns to catch up.
never: Chase the highest-returning fund to catch up.
Extend the date only for must-have goals.

check.q: Which is NOT a lever when a goal is off track?
check.why: Chase the highest-returning fund. Never chase returns to catch up.
